Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

marriage — the relationship of a married couple. Example: Their marriage is strong.
partner — the person you live with or love. Example: My partner cooks very well.
together — with each other. Example: We eat together every evening.
always — every time, 100%. Example: I always drink coffee in the morning.
usually — most of the time. Example: We usually walk to work.
sometimes — now and then, about 50%. Example: We sometimes eat out.
never — not at any time. Example: She never argues.
argue — to disagree in a strong way. Example: They argue about the washing-up.
support — to help someone. Example: We support each other.
share — to use something with another person. Example: We share the rent.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• We always ... together.
• I usually ...
• We sometimes argue.
• She never ...
• We support each other.

Grammar focus: Present simple for habits.
Use the present simple for habits and routines. Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb: We usually cook together. She never argues.

Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
My partner and I always eat together. We usually share the cooking and we sometimes argue about the washing-up. We never go to bed angry. We support each other.
